title: Biofuel Production Overview
desc: Understand how biofuels are made from crops, waste and algae, with sustainability, safety, cost and policy.
outcomes: Explain biofuel types and basic production steps.
Do simple mass and energy balances.
Write a balanced overview for a community or investor.
task: Produce a three-page overview of one biofuel pathway with process chart, balance, emissions estimate, risks and recommendation.
condition: A computer, public data, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor. No production work is done.
standard: Process steps and balances are correct; emissions use stated assumptions; risks and safety are listed; sources dated; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Students, farm cooperatives, energy staff, policy assistants.
evidence: process chart, balance sheet, emissions estimate, overview

ladder: Types of biofuel

L1: learner can name biofuel types. Focus module: Types of biofuel (Understand, 2 h). Liquid and gas fuels from biomass. Key points: Ethanol from sugar or starch; biodiesel from oils; biogas from waste. Advanced fuels from residues and algae. Blends: low blends are used in existing engines.

Teach: open with the worked example. Vegetable oil waste becomes biodiesel after a simple chemical step. Then set the activity: Make a type table. Mark against the standard: Each type has feedstock and use. Check at this level: Name three biofuels. Model answer: Ethanol, biodiesel, biogas. Table.
Feedstocks

L2: learner knows feedstock and hazard basics. Focus module: Feedstocks (Analyse, 2 h). What you start with matters. Key points: Food crops, residues, used oil, energy crops. Compare yield per hectare and competing uses. Prefer waste and residues.

Teach: open with the worked example. Used cooking oil avoids new land use. Then set the activity: Compare 4 feedstocks. Mark against the standard: Pros and cons for each. Check at this level: Best feedstock type? Model answer: Waste and residues. Compare.
Production steps

L3: learner can follow a process chart. Focus module: Production steps (Understand, 3 h). Basic process chain. Key points: Collect, clean, convert, separate, purify, store. Fermentation for ethanol; transesterification for biodiesel; digestion for biogas. Co-products such as glycerol or digestate.

Teach: open with the worked example. Digestate returns nutrients to the field. Then set the activity: Draw a process chart. Mark against the standard: Steps and outputs shown. Check at this level: What is a co-product? Model answer: Another useful output such as glycerol. Chart.
Mass and energy balance

L4: learner can do a simple balance. Focus module: Mass and energy balance (Apply, 3 h). Check the numbers. Key points: Inputs equal outputs plus losses. Energy out / energy in gives a ratio. Water use per litre.

Teach: open with the worked example. 100 kg oil gives about 95 kg biodiesel and 10 kg glycerol with alcohol. Then set the activity: Calculate a simple balance. Mark against the standard: Totals correct. Check at this level: What is a balance? Model answer: Inputs equal outputs plus losses. Sums.
Emissions and sustainability

L5: learner can estimate emissions. Focus module: Emissions and sustainability (Evaluate, 3 h). Cleaner only if the whole chain is clean. Key points: Count land change, fertiliser, processing energy and transport. Compare against fossil fuel per MJ. Use recognised methods.

Teach: open with the worked example. Waste-based fuel can cut emissions greatly; land-clearing crops may not. Then set the activity: Do a simple estimate. Mark against the standard: Method and sources listed. Check at this level: Name an emissions source in the chain. Model answer: Land change, fertiliser, processing, transport. Emissions.
Economics and policy

L6: learner can coordinate supply. Focus module: Economics and policy (Evaluate, 3 h). Costs, incentives and fairness. Key points: Feedstock is the largest cost. Incentives and blend mandates change prices. Fair prices for farmers and no food shortages.

Teach: open with the worked example. A mandate raises demand for used oil, so collection grows. Then set the activity: Cost one pathway. Mark against the standard: Currency shown. Check at this level: Name a safety hazard. Model answer: Flammable liquids or methanol. Supply.
Write the overview

L7: learner can audit an overview. Focus module: Write the overview (Create, 3 h). Balanced recommendation. Key points: Summary, evidence, risks, next steps. State what you do not know. Test with a reader.

Teach: open with the worked example. The note recommends biogas from market waste first. Then set the activity: Finish and present. Mark against the standard: Reader can repeat the choice. Check at this level: Name a quality test. Model answer: Water content, acidity, flash point. Peer audit.
